full_judgment:
4. In Writ Petition No. 2519 of 1998 the petitioner challenged the notice contained in সি-আই-ডি অফিস স্মারক নং কেন্দ্রীয় অপরাধ, সি-আই-ডি/২৫-৯৮(বিবিধ)1120 fJA 12-02-98 issued by respondent No. 5 Mr Md Fazlul Karim Khan, PPM Assistant Superintendent of Police CID Bangladesh Dhaka upon the petitioner along with 3 others asking them to appear before him on 27-7-98 at 10 AM in the morning with documents of land relating to CS Plot Nos. 72 and 73 of Mouza Mohakhali for interrogation in connection with application of one Mr Eklasur Rahman, Civilian Staff Officer Rehabilitation Directorate, Army Headquarter Dhaka Cantonment that since the petitioner was not within the country at that. time, an application praying for time on his behalf was filed by the learned Advocate, that the property measuring 1.66 acres in plot No. 87 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 207 and measuring 4.94 acres recorded in plot numbers 40, 72, 73, 74 and 75 of CS Khatian No 174 of Mouza Mohakhali originally belonged to the petitioner. The property was acquisitioned by the Government under Defence of India Rule 75A (2), that Mr ATM Mostafa Kamal recipient of the impugned notice in serial No.1 of the impugned notice along with others filed Writ Petition No. 2536 of 1995 in the High Court Division wherein the Rule was discharged by judgment dated 16th February, 1.998, against the judgment and order the petitioner moved Miscellaneous Petition for leave to Appeal No. 63 of 1998 before the Appellate Division and necessary steps are being taken for filing regular Civil petition, no notice containing the allegations was submitted by Mr Eklasur Rahman and the Miscellaneous petition is pending before the Appellate Division wherein the respondent No. 5 has nothing to do with the aforesaid land, that no criminal case was instituted against the petitioner by the respondent in any police station or court of Bangladesh, that notice issued by the respondent No. 5 is illegal and without jurisdiction. The impugned Notice is violative of the fundamental right of the petitioner and same has been issued only to humiliate and harass the petitioner. The petitioner having no other efficacious remedy moved this Court and obtained the Rule. 

 5. In Writ Petition No. 1765 of 1998 the petitioner challenged the, impugned action of respondent Nos. 2 to 5 asking the petitioner to appear before the Deputy Police Commissioner, Detective Branch, Dhaka Metropolitan City and produce document at 10 O'clock on 16-6-1998. In the Writ Petition it is alleged that on 14-6-98 at 9-30 AM an Inspector of Police named Md Abdullah, respondent No. 5 herein, accompanied by some police force arrested the petitioner from his residence and produced him before Mr Bazlul Karim. Deputy Commissioner, Detective Branch respondent No. 4 in the Writ Petition. The respondent No.4 asked the petitioner to produce the documents relating to the 15 kathas of land out of 4- 79 acres of land of CS plot Number 25, 26,24, 42 of CS Khatian Nos. 96, 97, 30 of Mouza Samair, Police Station Gulshan, District Dhaka and directed the petitioner to transfer the property to Mr Jamil Akhter and Kazi Nurjahan Alam, respondent Nos. 6 and 7 respectively, the petitioner was tortured mentally and he was directed to refund Taka 74,00,000 to the respondent Nos. 6 and 7, that the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 detained the petitioner in their office up to 4-30 PM and on the prayer of the petitioner he was freed and allowed 2(two) days time, that petitioner was asked by the respondent No.4 about Title Suit No. 290 of 1997 filed in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract for sale by Mr Khan Mohammad Ameer as plaintiff against the petitioner and the deed of agreement for sale of 4,79 acres of land to Khan Mohammad Amber. The petitioner was directed to transfer the said land to Khan Mohammad Amber on 16-6-98 when the petitioner again appeared before the respondent No. 4, the petitioner was directed by the respondent No. 4 again to appear on 21-6-96 with the documents of the land and he was threatened that in case he failed to produce the documents and refund the money to respondent Nos. 6 and 7 he would be put to inhuman torture. On 19-6-98 the petitioner filed an application to the Honourable Minister of Home Affairs praying for necessary action against the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 for creating fictitious bainapatra and trying to recover money from the petitioner illegally with the assistance of police of Detective Branch on 21-6-1998 when the petitioner appeared before the respondent No.4 he was again directed by the respondent No. 5 to produce the document and transfer the land to the respondent No.6 and 7 within seven days, but even then on 21-6-98 the petitioner was asked to transfer the land to the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 within 7(seven) days and the respondent No.4 gave threat that if he failed to comply with the verbal order he would be put to torture which might cause his death, that as the respondent Nos. 2-5 chased the petitioner and called him again and again to appear before him in their office and upon coming to know that he may be subjected to inhuman torture, the petitioner stayed out of his residence since 22-6-98. That despite repeated requests made by the petitioner the respondents did not serve any written notice or order upon the petitioner for his appearance and production of document, that no copy of allegation of the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 was served upon the petitioner who collected the copy of the allegation from the office of the Detective Branch, that over the self-same land the maternal uncle of the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 Mr Khan Mohammad Ameer as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 290 of 1997 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka against the petitioner for specific performance of contract and for permanent injunction and obtained order of status quo dated 26-1-98, that against the said order the petitioner filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 6 of 1998 before the High Court Division and by an order dated 11-2-98 the Appeal was admitted and record of the case was called for; that no Criminal Case was instituted against the petitioner in respect of alleged deed of agreement for sale by the respondent Nos. 6-7 in any court or in any police station of Bangladesh and that the High Court Division is in seisin of the subject matter in the First Appeal. The respondent No. 5 has no authority to enquire about the land to the petitioner and ask the petitioner to appear and submit document regarding his land. The action of the respondent Nos. 2-5 asking the petitioner to submit document in respect of certain land is illegal and without jurisdiction and it is violative of the fundamental right of the petitioner and the petitioner shall be humiliated and harassed in the hands of the respondents. The petitioner got no other effective and efficacious remedy by law. As such, he moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.
